1.The name of Shri Prashant Tiwari is printed int he cause list as opposite party no.2

, however,
neither he appeared nor any request has been sent to adjourn the case.

2. Heard Dinesh Kr. Chaudhary, learned counsel for the accused/applicant as well as learned A.G.A.
for the State and perused the record.
3.

This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Mehtab Alam Khan @ Monu for grant of bail, in Case Crime No. 73/2023, under Sections 363, 366, 376 IPC, and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Harraiya, District Balrampur, during trial.

4. Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that the accused-applicant has falsely been implicated in the instant case and he has not committed any offence as claimed by the prosecution.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the FIR of the instant case has been lodged by the father of the victim on 26.4.2023 at Police Station Harraiya, District Balrampur pertaining to the incident allegedly occurred on 30.3.2023 at 10. P.M. alleging that her daughter aged about 16 years has been enticed away by the applicant for the purpose of marriage.

On 26.4.2023 the prosecutrix was recovered with the applicant and her statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. were recorded, wherein she has not alleged any allegation against the applicant and has stated that the applicant is known to her for the last 2 years and they have solemnized 'Court Marriage' at Balrampur and and thereafter went to Maharashtra (Pune) and remained there for 20 days and when they got information that police is searching them, they returned.

6. It is also stated that the prosecutrix has stated in her statement recorded under Section 161, 164 Cr.P.C. that sexual relations between them has been established with her free will and consent.
7.

Highlighted the above facts, it is submitted that the prosecutrix has not levelled any allegation against the applicant and she stated that she had accompanied with the applicant with her free wish and will and sexual relation has been established with her consent.

8. It is further submitted that in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. the prosecutrix/
victim has categorically stated that she has educated up to Class-VIII and her date of birth is 8.4.2004 and her father has recorded wrong date of birth in her School.
9. It is further submitted that the applicant is in jail in this case since 26.04.2023 and he is not having any criminal antecedent.
There is no apprehension that the accused-applicant after release on bail, may flee from the process of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.

10. Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer for bail of the applicant on the ground that having regard to the age of the prosecutrix at the time and date of incident, she was not of consenting age and as such her statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. are irrelevant.

11. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. had categorically stated her date of birth as 8.4.2004 with further contention that her wrong date of birth has been recorded by her father in School.

It is on the basis of this date of birth (stated by the prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.), it is vehemently submitted on behalf of the applicant that at the date and time of the incident she was major.

Admittedly the prosecutrix/ victim has not alleged any allegation against the applicant and it is stated by her in categorical terms that sexual relations between them were established with her free wish and will.

The disputed question of facts may very well be adjudicated by the trial court, after providing opportunity to the parties to lead the evidence,
during the course of trial.
The applicant is in jail in this case since 26.4.2023 and he is not having any criminal history.
His presence may be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

12. Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion Mehtab Alam @ Monu vs State Of U.P. Thru. Secy. Deptt. Home ...

on the merits and demerits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

13. Let the applicant- Mehtab Alam Khan @ Monu involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
8. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
9. Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
10. Observations made herein-above are only for the purpose of disposal of bail application and the same shall not have any bearing on the trial of the case.
